title.narrative: Envelop 2: Strengthening health care provision in NWS

description.narrative:
This project aims to improve access to life-saving and life-sustaining coordinated, equitable health services for those most vulnerable and in need, Also, the project addresses human suffering in NWS by ensuring the sustainability of health services and improving the health conditions of those in need, including HC and IDPs across gender and age groups children, men, women, elderly, and PwDs.
To do so, UOSSM proposes a project including the provision of PHC services and filling critical gaps in secondary and specialized healthcare services, through:
- Supporting Al Skiekh Bahr PHC center (G0700127) in terms of running costs and medical supplies as it is already supported by GIZ in terms of staff salaries (33 staff). The center provides the services according to the revisited EHSP for 3000 beneficiaries with 4500 consultations per month. The PHC includes internal medicine, general medicine, midwifery, dental, pediatric, MHgap, nutrition, and bandage clinics. Also, the center will be provided with IPC means and will contribute to responding to cholera outbreaks by providing timely detection, referral, and case management of cholera by providing rapid access to oral rehydration solutions, and providing initial life-saving treatment for rehydration, referring severe cholera cases to CTUs/CTCs, and deliver health and hygiene education messages. The dehydration evaluation and the response will be conducted according to the NWS master case management and referral plan approved by the health cluster.
- Supporting Aqrpat hospital (G0703002), in terms of running costs and medical supplies as it is already supported by GIZ in terms of staff salaries (131 staff). The hospital, which is recognized by SBOMS as a training center for the orthopedic specialty, is the only hospital in NWS that provides orthopedic and reconstructive surgeries, diagnostics, emergency, and outpatient services, and prosthetics for PWDs, for almost 7600 beneficiaries with 9000 consultations per month.
- Supporting the inpatient unit of the psychological and mental health unit in Sarmada (G0703034), in terms of salaries and running costs, while the outpatient clinics are already supported by Relief International. The hospital, which is recognized by SBOMS as a secondary inpatient mental health care psychiatric facility, is the only unit that provides long-term specialized mental health in NWS. The inpatient unit will be staffed by 3 resident doctors, 9 nurses, and supervised by a psychiatrist, and has a capacity of 20 beds hospitalizing almost 15 unique patients (receiving 150 consultations per month) with severe mental health disorders, for 16-30 days until the patients present clear remission of the signs and symptoms of the acute episodes, in addition to proven stabilization levels based on the specialized psychiatrist clinical observation and supported with the Global Assessment of Function (GAF) scale scores.
